dual_degree_rules.description: General Institutional Requirements are the same for both degrees and are not repeated.

source.quote: General Institute Requirements will remain the same for both the degrees of the composite dual-degree program and therefore need not be repeated.

dual_degree_rules.description: Each degree's discipline requirements are met separately; a course meeting both degrees' discipline requirements is not repeated.

source.quote: While the Discipline Requirements of each of the two degrees in a dual degree program have to be met separately, any course that meets the discipline requirements of both the degree programs need not be repeated.

dual_degree_rules.description: Discipline electives of either degree may fulfil the open elective requirement of the other.

source.quote: In addition the Discipline Elective courses of either of the two degrees in a dual degree program may be used to fulfill the open elective requirement of the other degree.

dual_degree_rules.description: A PS-II or thesis is needed for each degree: 2 PS-II, 2 theses, or 1 PS-II + 1 thesis.

source.quote: A PS-II or Thesis must be done to meet the requirements of each degree. Therefore to complete the dual degree program a student must complete one of the following: 2 Practice School-II courses; 2 Thesis courses; 1 Practice School-II course and 1 Thesis course.

project_course_rules.description: At most 3 project courses count towards Discipline Electives, within the degree's discipline (or an allied one if the department says so), with sub-limits.

source.quote: A student may avail a maximum of 3 Project courses to meet the Discipline Electives Requirement under the head of (Discipline) Electives with the following limitations: (a) All of these Project courses should be (i) within the Discipline (for which the degree is being awarded) or (ii) from an allied Discipline if so specified by the Department offering the degree (b) The projects may be chosen from under these sub-heads. (i) Study Projects (maximum of 1) (ii) Laboratory (maximum of 2) (iii) Design Projects (maximum of 2) (iv) Special Projects (maximum of 1)

project_course_rules.note: Project codes: XXX F266 study, F366/F367 laboratory, F376/F377 design, F491 special (code processed/bulletin.json -> project_course_patterns).

project_course_rules.description: At most 3 project courses (any discipline) as Open Electives.

source.quote: A student may avail a maximum of 3 Project courses (under any of the heads mentioned above offered by any discipline as an Open Elective.

project_course_rules.description: At most 5 project courses in total against elective slots of any category.

source.quote: However, in total a student may avail at most 5 Project courses against Electives slots in any category.

huel_rules.description: A course (or its equivalent) of the student's own discipline(s) can't count as a HUEL, even if it is in the pool.

source.quote: It may be noted that a student cannot count a course (or its equivalent) of his/her own discipline (s) as a humanities elective even if it is listed in this pool of humanities electives.

huel_rules.description: Humanities electives are taken from the listed pool; the pool ends at SANS F111 and the 'Other Courses' after it are not HUELs.

minor_rules.description: Minor core at most 4 courses / 12 units; electives at least 2 courses / 6 units; total at least 5 courses / 15 units.

source.quote: Minor – Core 4 (max) 12 (max) Minor – Electives 2 (min) 6 (min) Minor – Total 5 (min) 15 (min)

minor_rules.note: Some minors ask for more (e.g. 6 courses / 18 units): minors[].min_courses / min_units in code processed/bulletin.json.

minor_rules.description: At most one project / seminar course towards a minor.

source.quote: A student may use at most one project / seminar type course to meet the requirements of a minor.

minor_rules.description: At most 2 courses (6 units) of a minor may be mandatory courses of the major (GIR excluding Humanities, or discipline core).

source.quote: At most 2 courses (and at most 6 units) out of the above requirement (of 5 courses and 15 units) may be met by mandatory courses of the student's degree i.e. major (or degrees i.e. majors) : i.e. from the general institutional requirement (excluding Humanities requirement) or the (Major) discipline Core(s).

minor_rules.description: No course counts for two minors, or for two majors and a minor.

source.quote: No course may be used to meet the requirements of two different minors nor may a course be used to the meet the requirements of two majors and a minor.

minor_rules.description: CGPA of at least 4.5 in the courses applied to the minor.

source.quote: A student – on completion of the requirements for a minor – must have maintained a cumulative GPA of 4.5 or above (out of 10) in the courses applied to the minor.

minor_rules.description: A minor is declared at the end of the 2nd year.

source.section: IV-129 Process for declaring / obtaining a minor
source.quote: A student – if he/she chooses to pursue a minor – must declare at the end of the 2nd year that he/she will pursue a specific minor.

minor_rules.note: At most one minor: Academic Regulations 7.37.
